system_prompt:
You are a strategy analyst investigating an opportunity for a manufacturer. Use these tools:
read_brief {} : read the company, the question and your budgets.
frame_problem {"objective":"...","constraints":["..."],"alternatives":["..."]} : state the real objective and the options, including ones the question did not suggest. Accepted once.
search_evidence {"query":"..."} : keyword search of the evidence. Uses one search.
challenge_theory {"theory_id":"T1","query":"..."} : search for evidence that could prove a theory wrong. Uses one search.
read_source {"id":"..."} : read a result found by search.
add_theory {"claim":"...","who_benefits":"...","why_behaviour_changes":"...","how_value_is_captured":"...","assumptions":["..."],"predictions":["..."]} : add one causal theory of value. Returns its id.
assess_evidence {"theory_id":"T1","evidence_id":"...","direction":"supports or contradicts or neutral","quote":"exact words from the source","evidence_kind":"company_assertion or customer_observation or independent_study or regulation or analogy or market_fact","does_not_show":"what this evidence cannot establish"} : say how evidence bears on a theory, honestly. Use neutral if it does neither.
propose_test {"name":"...","theories":["T1","T2"],"method":"...","sample":"...","measure":"...","prediction_by_theory":{"T1":"...","T2":"..."},"decision_rule":"...","cost_eur":N,"weeks":N} : design an experiment where the theories predict different results.
revise_theory {"theory_id":"T1","status":"kept or revised or rejected","reason":"...","new_claim":"the changed claim, or none","evidence_ids":["..."]} : update a theory after new evidence.
finish {"recommendation":"...","target_customer":"...","value_proposition":"...","favoured_theory":"T1","next_action":"...","uncertainty":"...","would_change_if":["..."],"evidence_ids":["..."]} : end the investigation.

Reply with one JSON object: {"name": "<tool>", "arguments": {...}}. A user turn that starts with "Tool result:" is the output of your call. End by calling finish.

Work like a scientist, not a consultant.
1. read_brief, then frame_problem. List at least three alternatives, including no expansion and options the question did not suggest.
2. Search before you theorise. Find out what the company already sells to individual buyers, and do not assume. Read at least three sources.
3. add_theory at least three times. A theory is a causal explanation of why people behave as they do, not advice. Do not write "the company should". Each theory needs a different cause: who benefits, why they would change behaviour, how the manufacturer captures value. Give assumptions, and predictions someone could measure.
For example, from eyewear: "People treat glasses as a medical necessity. If they came to see them as fashion, they would own several pairs, so a maker that controls design and retail could earn premium prices." A rival theory would name a different cause.
4. assess_evidence for every theory, quoting the source's exact words. Say what kind of evidence it is and what it cannot show. A company's own claim is not proof of demand. Use challenge_theory to look for evidence that could prove your favoured theory wrong. If you find nothing against it, say so. Never force a contradiction.
5. propose_test: an affordable experiment where the theories predict different results, with a decision rule that has a threshold.
6. If new evidence arrives, read it and use revise_theory.
7. finish. Say what you recommend, the next action, what is uncertain, and what would change your mind.

Never state a number or fact that is not in a source you read. Your theories are hypotheses, not facts. Results marked SIMULATED are not real demand, so never cite one in finish.

A controller opens the tools for each stage, and each tool result lists them. Before you finish you will also use:
state_position {"favoured_theory":"T1","recommendation":"...","confidence":"low or medium or high"} : say what you believe now. finish then also takes "confidence".
A SIMULATED result is a what-if exercise. Reason as if it were real, and say what it would mean for your theories. A result can change nothing. Still keep it out of the evidence you cite.

Individuals with ASD are willing to pay a premium for products that address their specific needs.
Moldex-Metric has the technical expertise and resources to develop and market specialized products.

Higher customer satisfaction and loyalty among this specific demographic.

arguments.why_behaviour_changes: Specialized products that cater to their specific hobbies will provide better comfort, functionality, and performance, leading to increased satisfaction and loyalty.
arguments.how_value_is_captured: Hellberg Safety can charge a premium price for these specialized products, increasing revenue and profitability.

arguments.claim: Consumers are increasingly aware of the long-term health effects of noise exposure and are seeking out high-quality hearing protection as a preventive measure. Hellberg Safety can capitalize on this growing awareness by positioning its products as essential safety gear.
arguments.who_benefits: Health-conscious consumers concerned about noise-induced hearing loss
arguments.why_behaviour_changes: As awareness of the dangers of noise exposure grows, consumers will be more inclined to invest in high-quality hearing protection to safeguard their long-term health.
arguments.how_value_is_captured: Hellberg Safety can command higher prices for its products by emphasizing their health benefits and positioning them as essential safety gear.
assumptions: There is a growing segment of consumers who are concerned about the long-term health effects of noise exposure.

predictions: Increased demand for Hellberg Safety's products among health-conscious consumers

Enhanced brand reputation as a provider of essential safety gear

arguments.why_behaviour_changes: By partnering with sports organizations, Hellberg Safety can gain exposure to a large audience of potential customers who are actively engaged in noisy environments. This visibility will increase brand awareness and drive demand.
arguments.how_value_is_captured: Hellberg Safety can secure exclusive partnerships, generate product sales, and potentially negotiate sponsorship deals, all while capturing valuable data on customer preferences and behavior.
assumptions: Sports organizations and event organizers are open to partnerships for hearing protection.
Participants and spectators at sporting events are a viable market for hearing protection products.
predictions: Increased brand visibility and awareness among sports enthusiasts and participants
Expansion into new markets and customer segments
Generation of additional revenue streams through product sales and sponsorship opportunities

results.title: Efficacy of pink noise and earplugs for mitigating the effects of intermittent environmental noise exposure on sleep
This is Hultafors Group
Prevalence of Hyperacusis and Its Relation to Health: The Busselton Healthy Ageing Study

result.title: Efficacy of pink noise and earplugs for mitigating the effects of intermittent environmental noise exposure on sleep
result.excerpt: Adding PN to EN worsened sleep structure, despite minor dose-dependent improvements of EN-induced sleep fragmentation and N3 sleep increases. Earplugs mitigated nearly all EN effects on sleep but started failing at the highest EN level (65 dBA).
